messages:
alex: Heads-up — prod token/sec dropped ~28% starting 2026-03-17 22:10 UTC after the r2026.03.17 release. Continuous-batcher queueing delays spiked, batches are sitting ~150-300ms longer than baseline.

maria: :eyes: Any CI/regression alerts?

ci-bot: [automated] perf/regression job failed: runtime/token-throughput. Regression detected on commit abc1234 (master -> r2026.03.17). Delta: -26% tokens/sec. Suggest bisect.

alex: I started a quick prod-staging profile. Repro on staging with the prod workload.

jonathan: Ran pprof on the batcher thread. Kernel selector is choosing memcpy fallback for several MLP kernels under long seqs after the selector heuristic change in PR #4526. That increases memcpy work and stalls the coalesce path.

alex: pprof snippet:

    30.2s  40.0% 40.0%  runtime.kernel_memcpy  
    18.1s  24.0% 64.0%  ContinuousBatcher::drain
    12.3s  16.3% 80.3%  KVPrefetch::handle_task

maria: KV cache hit-rate looks steady, but I see prefetch queue length climbing in the logs — tasks pile up and the batcher drain loop yields waiting on that queue. Log sample below:

    [2026-03-17T22:11:05Z] KVPrefetchTaskQueue: size=512 delay_ms=230
    [2026-03-17T22:11:07Z] BatchCoalesce: waiting_for_prefetch=true wait_ms=210

tasha: Repro steps I used: perf-driver with seq=4096, concurrency=64, workload mix: small->long tail. On staging the continuous-batcher drain latency jumped to 600-800ms intermittently and tokens/sec dropped ~30%.

ben: I started a bisect between commit range abc000..abc1234. Quick notes: reverting PR #4526 (kernel selector heuristic) restores tokens/sec to baseline on staging. Reverting the unrelated batching tweak (#4599) had no effect.

jonathan: So root cause looks like selector change that prefers a slower memcpy path for certain kernels at long seqs which interacts badly with our prefetch scheduling (prefetch tasks now hold resources longer). Combined effect -> queueing + token/sec drop.

alex: Proposed immediate mitigation: revert #4526 in prod (hotfix) and add a defensive guard in selector to keep previous policy for MLP kernels until we add perf tests. Also add a perf/regression test that runs long-seq + concurrency profile on CI.

maria: Agreed. I've opened revert PR r-4531 and added a canary plan (10% -> 50% -> 100% in 30m steps).

ci-bot: [automated] revert PR r-4531 created, CI checks green.

srebot: Deploy: revert r-4531 merged to canary at 22:45 UTC. Monitoring token/sec and batcher drain latency.

alex: Canary numbers: tokens/sec back to ~98-102% of baseline, batcher drain percentile P90 down from 780ms -> 210ms.

maria: Good. I'll keep the revert staged for full rollout pending 30m stable. Follow-up todo:
- add kernel-selector unit tests for fallback thresholds
- add end-to-end perf/regression harness that exercises prefetch queue depth
- update PR template to require perf note when touching kernel heuristics

ben: Also let's add an integration check that asserts KVPrefetchTaskQueue size stays < 200 under a synthetic load.

jonathan: I'll own the selector patch to re-introduce safer thresholds and add the unit tests.

alex: thanks everyone. Tagging for postmortem: ops impact minimal due to quick revert but we should file a short incident note and mark PR #4526 as blocked until fixes landed.

maria: filing the incident now. :thumbsup:

ben: small follow-up: consider moving prefetch work off the batcher hot path into background workers so a single slow kernel can't backpressure the coalescer.

alex: noted — that's medium-term. For now revert + tests is enough.

maria: closing loop — full prod rollout of revert started at 23:05 UTC, monitoring looks healthy.

alex: nice containment. We'll post a short summary in eng-runtime channel and link the PRs.

jonathan: will push selector patch branch and link to the incident doc.

maria: thanks all.
